papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Control for Smooth and Accurate Circular Trajectory Tracking in Mobile Robots
papers.summary: This paper investigates reinforcement learning-based control for smooth and accurate trajectory tracking of a nonholonomic mobile robot. Three reinforcement learning algorithms, Deep Q-Network (DQN), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), are implemented and evaluated, with conventional PID and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) controllers included as comparative baselines. The robot is modeled using unicycle kinematics, and the tracking task is formulated through body-frame longitudinal, lateral, and heading errors. papers.title: Physical AI Bridging the Digital Mind and the Material World
papers.summary: Physical AI is a pivotal moment in the interaction of machines with the physical world. It refers to a family of AI systems that interact with the physical world by integrating high-level models with sensors, actuators and control systems to perceive, reason, decide and act in the physical world. Physical AI, unlike generative or digital-only AI, that creates text, code or images within the confines of software, exists where what matters is measurable in motion, force and matter. papers.title: Active Microrobotic Sampling for Embodied Biological Digital Twins at the Limit STARLI Research Works Institute XXVIII Extension 06 English Description This high-density research monograph turns the biological digital twin from a passive recipient of measurements into an embodied experimental partner. Competing twins use uncertainty, expected information gain, physical reachability, safety, authorization, assay burden and traceability to propose the next microrobotic sampling location, time and analyte. The twin remains a versioned scientific belief rather than a replica of a patient, tissue or living system. Central Contribution The Active Sampling Evidence Charter binds twin ancestry, candidate and rejected actions, expected information gain, safety calculations, authorization state, robot trajectory, quantum and classical raw measurements, structured residuals, model forks, resets, abstentions and human overrides into one replayable evidence object. A quantum measurement qualifies only when it reduces biological sampling burden or improves mechanism discrimination against the best classical readout.
